name: Buffalo
operatingHours: NFTA Metro Rail runs ~5:10 AM–~12:50 AM on weekdays, ~7:00 AM–~12:50 AM on Saturdays and ~8:00 AM–~11:50 PM on Sundays and holidays. Trains every ~10 min at rush hour and every ~15–20 min otherwise. No overnight service.
fareInfo: NFTA Metro fare $2.00 (2026) on Metro Rail and buses; under-10s ride free. A day pass is $5. Pay with a MetGo smart card or the Token Transit app and fares cap at $5 a day, $25 a week or $75 a month. Buy single rides and passes at station ticket machines (cash or card). Riding the above-ground downtown stretch of Metro Rail (DL&W/Canalside to Fountain Plaza) is free.

hotels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Buffalo Downtown - Medical Ctr
Hotel at the Lafayette, Trademark Collection by Wyndham

sights.name: Frank Lloyd Wright's Martin House
sights.note: Wright's sprawling 1905 Prairie-style estate for a soap-company executive, restored with its art-glass windows, pergola and conservatory.
sights.hours: Guided tours Thu–Mon 9:30 AM–4:30 PM; closed Tue–Wed

sights.name: Canalside
sights.note: The rebuilt western end of the Erie Canal at the harbor, with boardwalks, replica canal channels, summer concerts and boat rentals, and winter skating on the frozen canals.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily; events and rentals vary by season

sights.name: Buffalo and Erie County Naval & Military Park
sights.note: Climb aboard a WWII destroyer, a guided-missile cruiser and a submarine moored at the waterfront, with a museum of military aircraft and vehicles beside them.
sights.hours: Daily 10:00 AM–4:00 PM in Oct (last ships ticket 3:00 PM); shorter or closed in winter. Below decks on USS The Sullivans are closed for preservation work.

sights.name: Buffalo AKG Art Museum
sights.note: A major modern and contemporary collection, from Pollock to Warhol, in a neoclassical temple joined to a glass Gundlach Building that opened in 2023.
sights.hours: Thu–Fri 10:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sat–Mon 10:00 AM–5:00 PM; closed Tue–Wed

sights.name: Forest Lawn Cemetery
sights.note: A rolling 269-acre garden cemetery with lakes, sculpture, a Wright-designed mausoleum and the grave of President Millard Fillmore.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily ~8:00 AM–5:00 PM (later in summer); main gate on Delaware Ave

sights.name: Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site
sights.note: The Wilcox Mansion where Roosevelt took the oath in 1901 after McKinley's assassination, told through guided, interactive tours.
sights.hours: Guided tours only: Mon–Fri hourly 9:30 AM–3:30 PM, Sat–Sun 11:30 AM–3:30 PM

sights.name: Buffalo City Hall
sights.note: A 32-story Art Deco tower from 1931 with a lavish lobby and a free 28th-floor observation deck over Lake Erie and downtown.
sights.hours: Observation deck Mon–Fri ~8:30 AM–4:00 PM; free building tour weekdays at noon

sights.name: Buffalo and Erie County Botanical Gardens
sights.note: A Victorian glass conservatory beside South Park with palms, cacti and seasonal flower shows.

sights.name: Buffalo Transportation Pierce-Arrow Museum
sights.note: A collection of Buffalo-built Pierce-Arrow luxury cars and other vehicles, plus a full-size Frank Lloyd Wright filling station built from his drawings.

sights.name: Elmwood Village
sights.note: A walkable strip of Victorian homes, indie shops, cafés and bars along Elmwood Avenue between Allentown and Delaware Park.
sights.hours: Shops ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM; bars open late

sights.name: Buffalo Zoo
sights.note: One of the oldest zoos in the US, compact and easy to walk, with polar bears, a rainforest house and an arctic exhibit at the edge of Delaware Park.

sights.name: Shea's Buffalo Theatre
sights.note: A gilded 1926 movie palace on Main Street that now hosts touring Broadway shows; it's worth seeing for the interior alone.
sights.hours: Performance evenings and matinees; box office weekdays

sights.name: Buffalo Museum of Science
sights.note: A hands-on science museum in a 1929 building with dinosaur, space and human-body galleries and an observatory dome.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 10:00 AM–4:00 PM, Sat–Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Delaware Park
sights.note: Olmsted's centrepiece park for Buffalo, with Hoyt Lake, a rose garden, the Japanese Garden and loop paths for walking or cycling.

sights.name: Richardson Olmsted Campus
sights.note: H. H. Richardson's twin-towered 1870s asylum on Olmsted-designed grounds, now home to the Lipsey Buffalo Architecture Center.
sights.hours: Grounds open daily; architecture center and tours on set days, check ahead

sights.name: Guaranty Building
sights.note: Louis Sullivan's 1896 early skyscraper, covered in ornate terracotta, with a free interpretive center in its restored lobby.
sights.hours: Lobby interpretive center open during building hours (~weekday daytime); free

sights.name: Larkin Square
sights.note: A revived factory-district plaza with weekly summer food-truck nights and live music among old brick warehouses.
sights.hours: Plaza open daily; events mainly Tue–Wed evenings May–Sep

sights.name: Niagara Falls State Park
sights.note: The American side of Niagara Falls, ~30 km north and not on Metro Rail: a car, a bus or a tour is needed. Paths run to Prospect Point, Goat Island and Terrapin Point.
sights.hours: Park open 24 h daily; falls are lit at night

railStations.name: Buffalo Exchange Street Station
railStations.note: Small downtown Amtrak station, rebuilt in 2020. Empire Service trains go to Albany and New York (~8 h) and to Niagara Falls, and the daily Maple Leaf runs to Toronto. A covered walkway under I-190 leads to Canalside Metro Rail station. The Lake Shore Limited to Chicago and Boston stops at Buffalo–Depew station in the suburbs instead.
railStations.hours: Opens around train times only; just a few trains a day, so check Amtrak timetables.

airports.name: Buffalo Niagara International Airport
airports.transitNote: Metro Rail doesn't go to the airport. NFTA bus 24 (Genesee; 24B all stops or the faster 24L, $2, not on this map) runs from the terminal to downtown in ~40–50 min, every 20–30 min. A taxi or rideshare takes ~20 min.
